PullRequest.Title: Agents window: add the Agents Launcher to start sessions from anywhere
PullRequest.Body:

Adds the **Agents Launcher**: a system-wide shortcut summons a small floating composer from any application, so you can start an Agents window session without switching to it. Similar features exist in other desktop AI apps: ChatGPT's Chat Bar, Claude's Quick entry and OpenClaw's Quick Chat.

No issue tracks this yet. It builds on the system-wide keybindings of the Agents window (#344954).

## What it does

- Opt in with a user keybinding; there is no default:
  ```jsonc
  { "key": "ctrl+space", "command": "workbench.action.agentsLauncher", "systemWide": true }
  ```
- **Enter** starts the session, hides the launcher, and opens the session in the Agents window.
- **Cmd+Enter** or **Alt+Enter** starts it in the background. The launcher stays open, with `Message sent ✓ Open Session` below the input.
- **Escape**, or switching away, hides the launcher and keeps the draft. The shortcut toggles it.
- **Show Agents Launcher** in an editor window asks the Agents window to show the launcher, opening the Agents window first if none is open, without bringing it to the front.

| Dark | Light |
| --- | --- |
| ![The Agents Launcher in a dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/main/vscode/347677-agents-launcher-dark.png) | ![The Agents Launcher in a light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/main/vscode/347677-agents-launcher-light.png) |

After Cmd+Enter, the launcher stays open with the status below the input ([video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/main/vscode/347677-agents-launcher-cmd-enter.mp4)):

![The Agents Launcher after Cmd+Enter, showing Message sent and Open Session below the input](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/main/vscode/347677-agents-launcher-cmd-enter.png)

## How it works

- The launcher is an always-on-top panel auxiliary window of the Agents window. On macOS it is an `NSPanel`, so showing it never activates the application. It hosts the existing new-session composer with a draft slot and `SessionHost` of its own, and is hidden rather than closed when dismissed.
- `AgentsLauncherPresenter` sequences each show: prepare, opacity 0, position, show, focus, wait for a rendered frame, opacity 1. Any later show or hide interrupts it, so a quick double press never leaves an invisible window with keyboard focus. Staying transparent until painted avoids a stale frame flashing on re-show.
- Every send is a background send, so a failed send gives its prompt back to the launcher. The new `INewSessionBackgroundSend.requestedInBackground` tells the launcher whether the user asked for a background send (stay open) or pressed Enter (leave for the Agents window).
- The Agents window owns the system-wide registration, as it does for Open Agents Window, so the shortcut keeps working with no editor window open.

## Changes outside the launcher

- `NativeHostMainService.positionWindow` no longer falls back to the calling window when the window a request targets has closed: a request for a closed auxiliary window moved its owner instead. The new `showWindow`, `hideWindow` and `setWindowOpacity` resolve their target the same way. Like the other native host methods that would reveal a window, `showWindow` does nothing in hidden-window mode (`--hidden-window`).
- Auxiliary windows gain `panel` and `opacity` open options.
- A new-session composer host can opt in with `hideChatWidgetWhileHidden`, so that its chat widget is visible only while the composer is. The launcher stays rendered while hidden, and its composer counted as a foreground chat, which suppresses chat tips. Only the launcher opts in; existing hosts keep their behavior.
- `INewSessionBackgroundSend` has a new required `requestedInBackground` field.
- `dom.getActiveDocument` (and so `getActiveWindow` and the layout service's active container) takes the window that received focus last, or that had focus as it registered, when several windows report focus. On macOS the launcher's panel takes focus without the Agents window losing it, so both report focus: popups of the launcher opened in the Agents window, and Close Window (Cmd+Shift+W) in the launcher closed the Agents window. With at most one window reporting focus, nothing changes.
- `ChatWindowComposerBackgroundSends` gives the prompt of an ordinary send back to its composer when the send does not start, such as when workspace trust is declined, without an error. Such sends (`requestedInBackground: false`) come only from hosts that send everything in the background, which today is only the launcher; chat windows' Send in Background is unchanged.

## Reviewing

Thirteen commits, each of which type-checks and passes its tests on its own. Read them in order:

1. Native host: ignore a window request whose target window has closed
2. Native host: show, hide and set the opacity of a window
3. Auxiliary windows: open as a panel and with an initial opacity
4. Sessions composer: let a host hide its composer's chat widget while hidden
5. Sessions composer: tell its host whether the user sent in the background
6. Agents Launcher: place its window and sequence its shows and hides
7. Agents Launcher: a floating new-session composer of the Agents window
8. Agents Launcher: open the session of an ordinary send in the Agents window
9. Agents Launcher: show it from editor windows
10. Agents window: own the system-wide keybindings of the Agents Launcher
11. Agents Launcher: hide after leaving it once a send or popup no longer defers it (from review)
12. Windows: take the window focused last as active when several report focus (from review)
13. Sessions composer: give back the prompt of an ordinary send that does not start (from review)

## How to test

1. Add the keybinding above to your user `keybindings.json` and open the Agents window.
2. Switch to another application and press the shortcut. The launcher appears near the top of the display under the pointer, with its input focused, and the other application stays active.
3. Type a prompt and press Cmd+Enter. The launcher stays open with `Message sent ✓ Open Session`; Open Session opens the session.
4. Type a prompt and press Enter. The launcher hides, and the Agents window comes to the front and opens the session.
5. Press the shortcut twice quickly: the launcher ends hidden. Escape hides it and keeps the draft. While it is open, change the color theme and the zoom level: it keeps its layout and fits its content.

## Validation

On every commit:

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed .ts files>`: passed
- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts <changed files>`: passed
- `node build/next/index.ts transpile`, then `./scripts/test.sh --run` for the launcher, `newChatWidget`, `chatWindowComposer`, `sharedChatInputComposer`, `openAgentsWindow.contribution`, `sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp` and both `agentSessionsActions` suites: passed (472 tests at the tip, including `dom`)

At the tip:

- `node build/stylelint.ts`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` for the composer hosts and the Agents window workbench (`dom`, `sessionView`, `workbench`, `chatEditor`, `mobileChatShell`, `mobileChatEditRow`, `newChatUserInteraction` and the suites above): 737 passed

Manually, in Code OSS on macOS, summoned like the global shortcut:

- Two toggles 0 to 120 ms apart, including while the window is created, always end hidden and unfocused.
- Theme change while open: the launcher keeps its styles.
- Zoom level 1: the window is 768×170 for 640×142 CSS pixels, with nothing clipped.
- Reopening: the window fits the composer on every show (142 px empty; 202 px with a five-line draft kept while hidden), also after Escape; clearing the draft while shown shrinks it back.
- The foreground chat count returns to 1 whenever the launcher hides; the Agents window's own composer still takes input.
- With the Agents window focused before the launcher shows, the launcher's mode picker opens in the launcher, and afterwards the Agents window's own picker opens in the Agents window.
- With both windows reporting focus (focus emulation over CDP, on the launcher's first show), the launcher's picker opens in the launcher, and Cmd+Shift+W closes only the launcher; the Agents window stays open, and the launcher's draft survives when it is summoned again.
- An Enter send whose preparation fails with `WorkspaceNotTrustedError` (injected with a conditional breakpoint) hides the launcher as usual and gives the prompt back to it, without an error notification. An Enter send with the same input sends exactly what was typed.
- Keyboard submit target: a key on a toolbar button keeps focus; a key in the input reclaims the submit target.
- Cmd+Enter keeps the launcher open with its status; Enter opens the started session in the Agents window.

Not run: Windows, Linux (including Wayland), VoiceOver, smoke and integration tests.

## Known limitations and follow-ups

- **Slow Enter sends:** after Enter, the launcher opens the session once it has started. If the user opens another session meanwhile, the started session still opens over it.

- **Cold start:** with only editor windows open, the shortcut opens the Agents window in the foreground before showing the launcher. Opening it without activating the application needs a hidden or minimized open in `windowsMainService`.
- **Gating:** system-wide keybindings run commands without preconditions. The editor-window command checks agent mode but not whether AI features are disabled; the Agents window checks AI features but not `chat.agent.enabled`.
- **Linux:** Electron does not support the cursor position or always-on-top on Wayland, nor window opacity on Linux. The launcher needs a fallback there, or should be gated.
- `src/vs/sessions/SYSTEM_WIDE_KEYBINDING.md` still describes the Agents window as owning Open Agents Window only.
- Clicking the Agents window while a picker of the launcher is open closes the picker, which gives focus back to its button and so to the launcher; the launcher then stays open. Switching to another application hides it as expected.
- Prompts of a send, such as workspace trust, show in the Agents window, which the always-on-top launcher can cover until it hides.
- The draft survives hiding, but not a reload of the Agents window.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The allocation count, loss of short-circuiting, per-character caller, and launcher-created multi-window trigger are all directly traced in code. Exact frame-time impact depends on GPU rendering use, line content, and auxiliary-window count, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: temporary JavaScript arrays plus repeated Document.hasFocus() calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With W registered windows, every getActiveWindow() call now scans all W windows and allocates both the Array.from result and the filtered result; callers such as viewLinesGpu invoke getActiveWindow() inside per-character loops, so a C-character range performs O(C*W) focus checks and O(C) extra allocations.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher CPU and GC pressure on rendering, selection, and hit-testing paths, causing avoidable frame or input latency in multi-window sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous implementation allocated one documents array and used find(), which stopped checking focus at the first focused document. Single-window sessions still took the existing fast path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed line maps every registered window and then filters the entire collection before another find, forcing a second array allocation and preventing focus checks from short-circuiting.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1090 replaces the prior one-array/short-circuit lookup with Array.from(...).filter(...), adding a filtered array and full-window scan to each multi-window call.
Findings.Title: Avoid materializing focused-window arrays in the hot active-window lookup
Findings.Impact: Once any auxiliary window is registered—including the launcher window that remains registered while hidden—GPU range calculations over long non-ASCII lines can allocate thousands of short-lived arrays and query every window's focus state once per character, increasing selection/render latency and GC churn.
Findings.Evidence: getActiveWindow() delegates to getActiveDocument(). The changed line uses Array.from(...).filter(...), whereas the deleted code used one Array.from(...).map(...) followed by a short-circuiting find(). In src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/viewLinesGpu/viewLinesGpu.ts, _visibleRangesForLineRange calls getActiveWindow().devicePixelRatio inside both character loops (lines 683 and 701), establishing a real per-character hot path. The new launcher keeps an auxiliary window registered after hide, so its normal warm state bypasses getActiveDocument's single-window fast path.
Findings.Recommendation: Check the last-focused registered window directly first, then use a single iterator pass for the fallback; avoid constructing either a windows list or a filtered list while preserving the last-focused semantics.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Ownership and disposal paths directly prove lifetime retention after first use. The exact retained byte count is not measured and the cache is intentionally bounded to one window, so the finding is low severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one native auxiliary window plus the complete NewChatView/ChatWidget DOM, input editor, scoped services, resize observer, and event subscriptions
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The retained set is bounded to one launcher per Agents window, but its cost persists for the entire remaining Agents-window lifetime after a single use, even if the launcher is never shown again.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Persistently elevated renderer/native-window memory and background subscription overhead after dismissal.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no launcher auxiliary window or launcher chat widget retained after use.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: hide() only hides the native window; the auxiliary window, full composer view, observer, and window-scoped disposables remain owned until Chat is disabled, AI is hidden, the user closes the auxiliary window, or the Agents window is disposed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 264 makes dismissal use presenter.hide(), which preserves the added auxiliary window and its complete rendered composer rather than disposing the window-owned resources.
Findings.Title: Evict the hidden launcher window after an idle period
Findings.Impact: A user who summons the launcher once and dismisses it keeps a full hidden chat UI and native auxiliary window alive for a potentially days-long Agents-window session, so process memory does not return to its prior baseline.
Findings.Evidence: _renderComposer creates a SessionHost, child instantiation service, and complete createNewChatView result and installs layout, keyboard, unload, and ResizeObserver listeners (lines 347-399). The presentation hide callback only calls native hide and view.setVisible(false) (lines 123-132), and this hide method returns that path without clearing _auxiliaryWindow or _windowDisposables. _destroyWindow, which actually disposes these resources, is only reached for disablement or service disposal (lines 510-526). The separate ChatWindowComposerModel owns the draft, so preserving the draft does not require retaining the rendered window indefinitely.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the composer model/draft, but dispose the auxiliary window and its window-scoped view after a bounded idle timeout; cancel that eviction on a quick re-show so warm-toggle latency remains fast.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window startup before the launcher is ever used
Scenarios.CriticalPath: WorkbenchPhase.BlockStartup constructs the IPC-listening contribution. The launcher service is registered with delayed instantiation, so auxiliary-window creation and composer rendering are off the startup critical path until the IPC handler or command accesses the service.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One contribution and one IPC listener per Agents window; independent of sessions, editors, or keybinding count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No queued or parallel expensive work; registration is synchronous and singular.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold startup installs only the handler. There is no launcher-window cache entry until first show.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contribution phase, delayed registration, and handler closure are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact cost of resolving the delayed-service proxy is not measured, but no window, filesystem, network, or provider operation is reached on startup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No startup finding; the heavyweight launcher UI remains lazy.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold global invocation, including invocation from an editor window when no Agents window is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor command crosses native-host IPC; main searches open windows and, on a cold miss, opens the Agents window, waits until it can receive the launcher IPC, then the Agents renderer queries cursor/display state, creates the auxiliary window, waits for styles, renders and measures the composer, and sequentially sets opacity, positions, shows, focuses, waits for a rendered frame, and restores opacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer-to-main request to locate or open the Agents window
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This launcher request and path did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the Agents renderer can receive the show request

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/load an Agents BrowserWindow when none is open
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one on a cold invocation; zero when an Agents window is already open
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No launcher invocation opened an Agents window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold invocation waits for the window to become ready enough to receive IPC

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Get cursor/display state, then set opacity, position, show/focus the native auxiliary window
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold or warm show performs one cursor query, up to two opacity calls, one position call, and one show call
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations and the rendered-frame wait are sequential on the visible-show critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical invocation; window search scales with the small number of top-level windows. Auxiliary-window and composer creation cardinality is one after coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: _windowCreation coalesces concurrent auxiliary-window creation. Presenter generations suppress stale show steps after prepare, though concurrent shows can each perform cursor lookup and preparation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold miss creates the Agents window if absent and one auxiliary launcher window. A warm invocation reuses both; failed/disabled preparation is not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all boundaries and coalescing behavior are explicit in the changed call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native window creation and style-load duration vary by platform and machine; the call chain and sequential critical path are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding for inherent cold feature creation; creation is lazy and coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Warm launcher toggles, content resizing, and dismissal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A warm show reuses the auxiliary window, makes the view visible, synchronously measures content, then performs native opacity/position/show operations and waits for paint. ResizeObserver callbacks synchronously read geometry and send a positionWindow IPC only for a distinct rounded bound. Hide sends native hide and marks the chat widget invisible after completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Move/resize the native auxiliary window after a content-height change
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per distinct computed bound after ResizeObserver batching and equality suppression
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the resize callback but not by typing itself; native resize can trigger another layout delivery

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hide the auxiliary native window without closing it
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hide completion precedes marking the embedded chat widget invisible

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One sequence per show/hide; resize IPC cardinality follows distinct content-height changes, typically line-count or status-row changes rather than every keystroke.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Presenter generations interrupt stale show sequences. Resize callbacks are not explicitly serialized, but ResizeObserver batches DOM changes and equalBounds suppresses unchanged bounds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The auxiliary window and full rendered NewChatView are a warm cache with no idle eviction; they survive every hide until disablement, explicit close, or Agents-window disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the hide and destroy ownership paths prove the complete window/view survives indefinitely after first use.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact retained bytes for the native window, DOM, editor, and services are platform-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the no-eviction warm cache because one use retains the full hidden window and chat UI for the rest of the Agents-window lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents-window editor rendering after an auxiliary window is registered, including while the launcher is hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hot rendering, selection, and hit-testing callers invoke getActiveWindow(), which delegates to getActiveDocument(). With more than one registered window, the changed lookup materializes and filters all windows instead of taking the single-window fast path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with hot-call count C and registered windows W. GPU visible-range calculation calls getActiveWindow inside per-character loops for non-basic-ASCII text, making the changed scan O(C*W) and adding one filtered-array allocation per character.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on the UI/rendering thread; no limiter or deferral is possible once invoked.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result is cached. The launcher remaining registered while hidden keeps this path warm but permanently outside the single-window fast path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed allocation pattern and per-character caller are directly present in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prevalence depends on GPU rendering, non-ASCII line length, and number of auxiliary windows; the added allocation and scan multiplicity are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the allocation/full-scan regression because it adds CPU and GC work to a proven per-character rendering path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submitting an ordinary or background launcher prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing NewChatWidget dispatches one new-session request through the sessions management/provider path. An ordinary send additionally hides the launcher and focuses the Agents window, then opens the started session; a requested background send keeps the launcher open. The added requestedInBackground field only routes recovery/open behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one new-session request to the configured session provider, which may start a local or remote agent
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per user submission, independent of attachment count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing provider request path existed, but there was no launcher workflow invoking it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The session must start before an ordinary send opens it; requested background sends continue without opening it

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hide the launcher and force-focus the Agents window around an ordinary send
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one hide/focus sequence per ordinary send
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hide/focus occurs as the send leaves; session opening waits for the provider request to report started

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One provider request and one tracking entry per submitted prompt; attachments are shallow-copied once as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each send is independently tracked until its request ends; the PR does not add a per-item fan-out loop or aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new request cache. Composer draft/model state persists; failed ordinary sends can restore their captured prompt.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for one-request cardinality and launcher IPC; provider implementation details vary but are unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and whether work is local, subprocess-backed, or network-backed depend on the selected provider.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: metadata propagation does not increase provider call cardinality, attachment copying, or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 28 changed files. Submitted two findings: hot multi-window active-document lookup now performs a full scan and extra allocation on proven per-character rendering callers, and the launcher warm cache retains its complete hidden auxiliary window/chat UI without idle eviction. Cold creation is lazy/coalesced, resize IPC is equality-suppressed, and send metadata does not add boundary fan-out.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
